ads.name: LP_C01_NightSheLooked
ads.title: The Night She Looked
ads.creative: Kitchen table at night, bank statements spread out, coffee cup, pen, book on the pile. Imagery ready.
primary: Her banker asked one question she could not answer.
Your revenue is up twelve percent. Your cash is down twenty. Why?
She had no idea.
That night she spread twelve months of bank statements across her kitchen table. Her P&L said she was fine. Her bank account said something else.
It was not good news. But it was a list.
And you can fix a list. You cannot fix a feeling.
$21. A hundred days to get it back.
ads.headline: Revenue Up 12%. Cash Down 20%.
ads.description: The fear is worse than the truth. Every single time.

ads.name: LP_C02_ToolNotSystem
ads.title: The Tool Is Not The System
ads.creative: Hand holding the paperback against a plain white wall. Imagery ready.
primary: QuickBooks, set up years ago and never properly maintained.
Most owners buy it, watch a few tutorials, and then wonder why nothing got better.
The tool is not the system. A tool without a system is just expensive software.
This is not an accounting book. No debits and credits. No lecture.
It is for owners doing $250K to $5M a year who are great at the work and were never taught the money side.
ads.headline: The Tool Is Not The System
ads.description: You bought the software. Nothing changed.

ads.name: LP_C03_CouldNotProve
ads.title: She Could Not Prove It Was Good
ads.creative: Jackie seated, holding the book, direct eye contact, office background. Imagery ready, subject to the 9:16 crop lift and a cover subtitle check at 100%.
primary: The bank said no.
Not because her business was bad. Because she could not prove it was good.
She brought a P&L from six months ago and a balance sheet she could not explain.
A year and a half later she walked back in with numbers she could explain. She got the loan.
Same business. Same owner. She could just see it now.
ads.headline: She Could Not Prove It Was Good
ads.description: Approved on the first ask, not the third.

ads.name: LP_C04_TenErrors
ads.title: Ten Errors in the First Month
ads.creative: Jackie across a desk from a client, pen in hand, taking notes. Imagery ready.
primary: She had a part time bookkeeper who did the minimum.
She put the change off for more than a year. She was sure the clean up would be brutal.
It took a month.
In that first month I found ten errors her last bookkeeper had made.
She had not been careless. She had been paying someone who did the minimum, and she had no way to check.
Simple, efficient and stress free. Her words, not mine.
ads.headline: Ten Errors in the First Month
ads.description: She put it off a year. It took four weeks.

ads.name: LP_C06_ElevenCharges
ads.title: Eleven Charges
ads.creative: Designed piece, data style. Eleven line items stacked like a printed bank statement column, eight struck through, three circled by hand. Imagery ready.
primary: She found eleven charges she did not recognize. Every month. Some had been running for years.
Eight were subscriptions she had forgotten about. She cancelled all eight in a week. It took her under an hour.
The other three were vendors who had quietly raised their prices. She called them. Two gave her a discount.
That is one hour of one step. There are seven.
ads.headline: Eleven Charges She Did Not Recognize
ads.description: Eight cancelled in a week. Under an hour.

ads.name: LP_C07_ThreeNumbers
ads.title: The Three Numbers
ads.creative: Designed piece, sparse. Three blank ruled lines labelled REVENUE, EXPENSES, IN THE BANK, nothing filled in. Imagery ready.
primary: Here is something you can do tonight. It is free and it takes thirty minutes.
Write down three numbers from memory. Your monthly revenue. Your monthly expenses. What is in the bank right now.
Then go and check all three.
The gap between what you wrote and what is really there is the part of your business you are running blind.
Do not fix it. Do not judge it. Just look.
That is step one of seven. It takes thirty minutes and costs nothing.
ads.headline: Three Numbers. Thirty Minutes.
ads.description: Do not fix it. Do not judge it. Just look.

ads.name: LP_C08_TwoKinds
ads.title: Two Kinds of Owner
ads.creative: Photo of Jackie, three quarter frame, with clear space to one side for the overlay line: looking profitable and being profitable are two different businesses. Imagery to produce, Jackie then designer.
primary: Someone at a networking dinner brings up profit margins. Most owners I meet nod along and hope nobody asks what theirs are.
There are two kinds of business owner. The ones working flat out to look profitable. And the ones who know they are.
The difference is not how hard they work. It is what they can see.
Seven steps. Read it in an evening.
ads.headline: Two Kinds of Business Owner
ads.description: The difference is not effort. It is visibility.

ads.name: LP_C09_NeverShowedHer
ads.title: Her Bookkeeper Never Showed Her
ads.creative: Closed manila folder of unopened statements with the book on top, shot from directly overhead in cool daylight. Imagery to produce, Jackie.
primary: Her bookkeeper made a cash flow statement every month. Filed it away. Never showed it to her.
She found out it existed when the bank asked for it.
She had never seen one in her life. The loan was declined.
Nobody had cheated her. He was doing the job he was hired to do. Nobody had ever been hired to explain any of it to her.
ads.headline: Her Bookkeeper Never Showed Her
ads.description: She found out it existed when the bank asked.

ads.name: LP_C10_WednesdayCall
ads.title: The Wednesday Call
ads.creative: Phone face down on a desk beside the book, dim office at dusk. Imagery to produce, Jackie.
primary: A competitor called on a Wednesday and offered to buy his business.
He said he would think about it. Then he opened his books.
Everything was current. The business could run without him for a month. He knew what it was worth.
He said no.
The point is that he could have said yes.
ads.headline: A Competitor Offered to Buy It
ads.description: He said no. The point is he could have said yes.
